+"""Phase 7 approval checker specification (16 cases, expected RED until tools land)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+from cases import (
+    APPROVAL_CASES,
+    APPROVAL_TEST_CONTENT,
+    APPROVAL_TEST_PATH,
+    REGISTRY_CONTENT,
+)
+from harness import run_approval
+
+CASES = APPROVAL_CASES
+RECORD_PATH = "docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-04-governance.txt"
+REGISTRY_PATH = "docs/req/requirements.yaml"
+
+
+def _digest(content: str) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _aggregate(file_digest: str) -> str:
+    line = f"{file_digest}  {APPROVAL_TEST_PATH}\n"
+    return hashlib.sha256(line.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _record(
+    test_commit: str,
+    *,
+    file_digest: str,
+    aggregate: str,
+    approved_by: str = "A (@yuxiangdu39)",
+    approved_at: str = "2026-11-22T00:00:00Z",
+    reviewed_head: str | None = None,
+    requirement: str = "FR-04",
+    omit_reviewed_head: bool = False,
+    omit_approved_by: bool = False,
+    omit_aggregate: bool = False,
+) -> str:
+    reviewed = reviewed_head if reviewed_head is not None else test_commit
+    lines = [
+        "PR/task: FR-04 governance tools",
+        f"requirement: {requirement}",
+        "branch: spec/FR-04-governance-tools",
+        f"test_content_commit: {test_commit}",
+        f"merge_commit: {test_commit}",
+    ]
+    if not omit_reviewed_head:
+        lines.append(f"reviewed_pr_head: {reviewed}")
+    lines.append("files (per-file SHA-256):")
+    lines.append(f"  {file_digest}  {APPROVAL_TEST_PATH}")
+    if not omit_aggregate:
+        lines.append("aggregate_sha256:")
+        lines.append(f"  {aggregate}")
+    if not omit_approved_by:
+        lines.append(f"approved_by: {approved_by}")
+    lines.append(f"approved_at: {approved_at}")
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def build_approval_repo(case, git_repo):
+    root_commit = git_repo.commit({"README.md": "root\n"}, "root")
+    test_commit = git_repo.commit(
+        {
+            APPROVAL_TEST_PATH: APPROVAL_TEST_CONTENT,
+            REGISTRY_PATH: REGISTRY_CONTENT,
+        },
+        "tests",
+    )
+    file_digest = _digest(APPROVAL_TEST_CONTENT)
+    aggregate = _aggregate(file_digest)
+
+    scenario = case.scenario
+    approved_by = "A (@yuxiangdu39)"
+    approved_at = "2026-11-22T00:00:00Z"
+    reviewed_head: str | None = None
+    requirement = "FR-04"
+    omit_reviewed = False
+    omit_approved = False
+    omit_aggregate = False
+    author = "ZFebron491001"
+
+    if scenario == "pending":
+        approved_by = "PENDING"
+        approved_at = "PENDING"
+    elif scenario == "self_approval":
+        author = "yuxiangdu39"
+    elif scenario == "unknown_requirement":
+        requirement = "FR-99"
+    elif scenario == "hash_mismatch":
+        file_digest = "0" * 64
+        aggregate = _aggregate(file_digest)
+    elif scenario == "aggregate_mismatch":
+        aggregate = "0" * 64
+    elif scenario == "reviewed_head_missing":
+        omit_reviewed = True
+    elif scenario == "approved_by_missing":
+        omit_approved = True
+    elif scenario == "record_malformed":
+        omit_aggregate = True
+    elif scenario == "reviewed_head_not_ancestor":
+        reviewed_head = "f" * 40
+
+    record = _record(
+        test_commit,
+        file_digest=file_digest,
+        aggregate=aggregate,
+        approved_by=approved_by,
+        approved_at=approved_at,
+        reviewed_head=reviewed_head,
+        requirement=requirement,
+        omit_reviewed_head=omit_reviewed,
+        omit_approved_by=omit_approved,
+        omit_aggregate=omit_aggregate,
+    )
+
+    if scenario != "missing_record":
+        record_commit = git_repo.commit({RECORD_PATH: record}, "approval record")
+    else:
+        record_commit = test_commit
+
+    if scenario == "test_drift":
+        head = git_repo.commit(
+            {
+                APPROVAL_TEST_PATH: "def test_fixture():\n    assert False\n",
+            },
+            "test drift",
+        )
+    elif scenario == "extra_test_changed":
+        head = git_repo.commit(
+            {
+                "src/egta/risk_gate/impl.py": "x = 1\n",
+                "test/offline/governance/extra_test.py": "def test_extra():\n    assert True\n",
+            },
+            "impl plus test",
+        )
+    else:
+        head = git_repo.commit({"src/egta/risk_gate/impl.py": "x = 1\n"}, "impl")
+
+    if scenario == "test_base_missing":
+        base = root_commit
+    elif scenario == "missing_record":
+        base = test_commit
+    else:
+        base = record_commit
+    registry: str | Path = git_repo.path / REGISTRY_PATH
+    if scenario == "missing_registry":
+        registry = git_repo.path / "docs/req/missing.yaml"
+    return record_commit, base, head, registry, author
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES, ids=[case.test_id for case in CASES])
+def test_approval(case, git_repo):
+    _, base, head, registry, author = build_approval_repo(case, git_repo)
+    result = run_approval(
+        git_repo,
+        RECORD_PATH,
+        base,
+        head,
+        registry,
+        author=author,
+        json_output=case.json_output,
+    )
+    output = result.stdout + result.stderr
+    assert result.returncode == case.expected_exit, (
+        f"{case.test_id}: expected exit {case.expected_exit}, "
+        f"got {result.returncode}\n{output}"
+    )
+    if case.expected_code is not None:
+        assert case.expected_code in output, (
+            f"{case.test_id}: expected code {case.expected_code!r}\n{output}"
+        )
+    if case.json_output and result.returncode == 0:
+        payload = json.loads(result.stdout)
+        assert payload["ok"] is True

+"""Meta-test: validate the Phase 7 governance test manifest without the tools."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from cases import ALL_GOV_CASES, APPROVAL_CASES, CASES_BY_CATEGORY, PERM_CASES
+
+EXPECTED_COUNTS = {"PERM": 16, "APPR": 16}
+MODULES = {
+    "PERM": "test_permissions",
+    "APPR": "test_approval",
+}
+REQUIRED_REQUIREMENTS = {"GATE-01", "GATE-02", "NFR-07", "D3"}
+ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^T-GOV-(PERM|APPR)-\d{2}$")
+ALLOWED_STATUSES = {0, 1}
+
+
+def test_manifest_has_32_unique_cases():
+    assert len(ALL_GOV_CASES) == 32
+    ids = [case.test_id for case in ALL_GOV_CASES]
+    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))
+    for case in ALL_GOV_CASES:
+        assert ID_PATTERN.match(case.test_id), case.test_id
+
+
+def test_manifest_category_counts_and_coverage():
+    assert set(CASES_BY_CATEGORY) == set(EXPECTED_COUNTS)
+    for category, expected in EXPECTED_COUNTS.items():
+        cases = CASES_BY_CATEGORY[category]
+        assert len(cases) == expected, category
+        assert any(case.classification == "positive" for case in cases), category
+        assert any(case.classification == "negative" for case in cases), category
+    covered = {
+        requirement
+        for case in ALL_GOV_CASES
+        for requirement in case.requirement_ids
+    }
+    assert covered >= REQUIRED_REQUIREMENTS
+
+
+def test_manifest_fields_are_complete():
+    for case in ALL_GOV_CASES:
+        assert case.requirement_ids, case.test_id
+        assert case.description, case.test_id
+        assert case.expected_exit in ALLOWED_STATUSES, case.test_id
+        assert (case.expected_code is None) or isinstance(case.expected_code, str)
+        assert case.classification in {"positive", "negative"}, case.test_id
+        assert case.failure_mode, case.test_id
+        if case.classification == "positive":
+            assert case.expected_exit == 0, case.test_id
+        else:
+            assert case.expected_exit != 0, case.test_id
+
+
+def test_every_case_is_wired_to_one_test_module():
+    wired = []
+    for category, module_name in MODULES.items():
+        module = importlib.import_module(module_name)
+        assert list(module.CASES) == list(CASES_BY_CATEGORY[category]), module_name
+        wired.extend(module.CASES)
+    assert [case.test_id for case in wired] == [case.test_id for case in ALL_GOV_CASES]
+
+
+def test_permission_and_approval_manifests_are_distinct():
+    assert len(PERM_CASES) == 16
+    assert len(APPROVAL_CASES) == 16
+    assert not ({case.test_id for case in PERM_CASES} & {case.test_id for case in APPROVAL_CASES})

+class Violation:
+    code: str
+    message: str

+    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:

+

+    test_content_commit: str
+    reviewed_pr_head: str

+    approved_by: str
+    approved_at: str
+    requirement: str
+    files: dict[str, str]

+        result = subprocess.run(
+            ["git", "-C", str(repo), *args],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            errors="replace",
+        )
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise CheckerError(f"git unavailable: {exc}") from exc
+    if check and result.returncode != 0:
+        message = result.stderr.strip() or f"git {' '.join(args)} failed"
+        raise CheckerError(message)

+
+

+    result = _git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{revision}^{{commit}}", check=False)

+
+

+    result = _git(

+        message = result.stderr.strip() or "git merge-base --is-ancestor failed"

+        approved_by=fields.get("approved_by", "").strip(),

+        ]

+            ]

+                    "TEST_DRIFT",
+                    f"approved test content changed in the implementation: {path}",
+                )
+            ]

+
+
+def _emit(violations: Sequence[Violation], json_output: bool) -> None:
+    if json_output:
+        payload = {
+            "ok": not violations,
+            "violations": [violation.as_dict() for violation in violations],
+        }

+        return

+        print("OK: approval record verified")
+        return
+    for violation in violations:
+        print(f"{violation.code}: {violation.message}")
+
+
+def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--repo", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--record", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--implementation-base", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--implementation-head", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--registry", required=True)

+    raise SystemExit(main())

+0 clean, 1 violation, 2 tool or usage error.

+    if role == "plan":

+    if path.startswith(PROTECTED_PREFIXES) or path == "CODEOWNERS":
+        return "PROTECTED_PATH"

"""Pack-level tests for FR-01 / INV-02, driven by the E-01..E-31 fixtures.

This is the **spec / test-first** artifact (GATE-01). It fixes the observable
behaviour of ``egta.evidence.pack.build_pack`` and ``validate_claims`` before any
implementation exists. It stays RED on the spec branch because ``egta.evidence``
does not yet provide ``InvalidCitation`` / ``egta.evidence.pack`` — the evidence
contract types are already on main (B's PR #21 merged at ``141547a``). The
implementation PR must descend from this spec's merge commit.

Post-#21 the RED is ``ImportError: cannot import name 'InvalidCitation' from
'egta.evidence'`` (33 errors / 20 functions / 33 cases), not a missing
``egta.contracts``.

Import strategy: the contract/implementation imports are performed *inside* a
session-scoped fixture, not at module import. That keeps the module collectable
under ``pytest -m "not spec"`` (so the existing ``test/offline/evidence`` suite
still collects cleanly) while ``pytest -m spec`` reaches the fixture and fails
there with a clear RED. A module-level import would abort collection for *every*
selection and break ``-m "not spec"``.

Scope: only the pack-level outcomes that the time-policy suite left "carried as
data". Pure time filtering (E-13..E-20, E-27, E-28, E-31) is already asserted by
``test_time_policy.py`` and is not re-tested here; a small representative slice is
re-checked through the pack API to prove time filtering is wired in.

Frozen decisions (resolved from D's review of #25):

* ``pack_hash`` is **computed by ``build_pack``**, never supplied by the caller.
  It is a 64-hex digest, deterministic for identical input, and content-bound
  (changing an item changes it). It must equal A's ``build_pack`` output being
  identical to ``egta.risk_gate.canonical.recompute_evidence_hash(pack)`` over
  the pack's ``evidence_fields`` — this is asserted by
  ``test_pack_hash_matches_risk_gate_canonical`` (a real A->D integration check
  against the helper already on main), not merely by "some deterministic
  digest". The concrete algorithm is frozen by that equality; if the shared
  helper changes, this test and the implementation must change together.
* ``validate_claims`` accepts **full** evidence ids
  (``<run_id>-<case_local_id>``), matching the risk gate's index
  (``risk_gate/rules.py``) — not the fixture's case-local ids.
* A dangling citation raises the concrete ``egta.evidence.InvalidCitation``
  (a ``ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION`` error), and the message names the bad id.
* E-22 ``conflict_group`` is supplied explicitly by the caller; the test asserts
  the group equals the supplied key (no underivable label is frozen).
* E-26 staleness is frozen as "``source_type == 'cache'`` is always stale"
  (no freshness threshold in this spec), with a fresh non-cache control.
* ``pack.items`` preserves input order (admitted items only).

Fixture -> assertion map:

    normal admit    E-01 E-02 E-03 E-04 E-05 E-06 E-08 E-09 E-10 E-12
    field mapping   E-01 E-07 E-10 (raw -> EvidenceItem source_uri/published_at/
                    fetched_at/excerpt/trust_label/content_hash)
    time wired in   E-07 (date-only admitted), E-16/E-17 (future/undated excluded)
    dedupe          E-21  (only E-21-1 survives; E-21-2 neither admitted nor excluded)
    conflict        E-22  (both retained, same caller-supplied conflict_group)
    tampered        E-23  (E-23-2 excluded INTEGRITY_VIOLATION, E-23-1 kept),
                    E-30  (single item excluded INTEGRITY_VIOLATION)
    provider fail   E-24, E-25 (items=[], provider exclusion VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE/unreachable)
    stale cache     E-26  (item excluded STALE_DATA/stale, never available)
    citation        E-29  (pack builds, validate_claims raises InvalidCitation)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date

import pytest

pytestmark = pytest.mark.spec


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def pack_api():
    """Import the contract types and the (to-be-implemented) pack API once.

    RED on the spec branch: this raises ``ImportError`` because ``egta.evidence``
    does not provide ``InvalidCitation`` and ``egta.evidence.pack`` does not
    exist yet (A implementation unmerged). The contract types themselves are
    already importable (B #21 merged). Importing here rather than at module scope
    keeps ``-m "not spec"`` collection clean.
    """
    from egta.contracts import (  # noqa: F401
        Availability,
        EvidenceItem,
        EvidencePack,
        ExcludedItem,
        RunSpec,
    )
    from egta.contracts.events import ReasonCode  # noqa: F401
    from egta.evidence import InvalidCitation  # noqa: F401
    from egta.evidence.pack import build_pack, validate_claims  # noqa: F401

    class _Api:
        pass

    api = _Api()
    api.Availability = Availability
    api.EvidenceItem = EvidenceItem
    api.EvidencePack = EvidencePack
    api.ExcludedItem = ExcludedItem
    api.RunSpec = RunSpec
    api.ReasonCode = ReasonCode
    api.InvalidCitation = InvalidCitation
    api.build_pack = staticmethod(build_pack)
    api.validate_claims = staticmethod(validate_claims)
    return api


def _run_spec(api, frozen_now, case: dict):
    """Build a RunSpec whose as_of equals the case's as_of instant."""
    return api.RunSpec(
        schema_version="1.0",
        run_id=f"run-{case['case_id']}",
        ticker="AAPL",
        as_of=case["as_of"],
        mode="enhanced",
        model_config_hash="1" * 64,
        prompt_hash="2" * 64,
        policy_hash="3" * 64,
        snapshot_id=f"snap-{case['case_id']}",
        limits={},
    )


def _full_id(run_spec, case_local_id: str) -> str:
    return f"{run_spec.run_id}-{case_local_id}"


def _admitted_local_ids(pack, run_spec) -> list[str]:
    prefix = f"{run_spec.run_id}-"
    return [item.evidence_id[len(prefix):] for item in pack.items]


def _build(api, load_case, frozen_now, case_id: str, *, conflict_key=None):
    case = load_case(case_id)
    run_spec = _run_spec(api, frozen_now, case)
    kwargs = {}
    if "provider_error" in case:
        kwargs["provider_error"] = case["provider_error"]
    if conflict_key is not None:
        kwargs["conflict_key"] = conflict_key
    pack = api.build_pack(run_spec, case["items"], **kwargs)
    assert isinstance(pack, api.EvidencePack), case_id
    return case, run_spec, pack


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Normal admission + raw -> EvidenceItem field mapping
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

NORMAL_CASES = ["E-01", "E-02", "E-03", "E-04", "E-05", "E-06", "E-08", "E-09", "E-10", "E-12"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case_id", NORMAL_CASES)
def test_normal_items_admitted(pack_api, load_case, frozen_now, case_id):
    api = pack_api
    case, run_spec, pack = _build(api, load_case, frozen_now, case_id)

    expected = case["expected"]["admitted"]
    assert _admitted_local_ids(pack, run_spec) == expected
    assert pack.excluded_items == []
    assert pack.run_id == run_spec.run_id
    assert pack.snapshot_id == run_spec.snapshot_id
    assert pack.cutoff == run_spec.as_of

    for item in pack.items:
        assert isinstance(item, api.EvidenceItem)
        assert item.availability == api.Availability.AVAILABLE
        # INV-02: an admitted item carries no refusal code.
        assert item.reason_code is None


FIELD_MAPPING_CASES = ["E-01", "E-07", "E-10"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case_id", FIELD_MAPPING_CASES)
def test_raw_fields_map_to_evidence_item(pack_api, load_case, frozen_now, case_id):
    """FR-01 core: every traceability field survives raw -> EvidenceItem intact."""
    api = pack_api
    case, run_spec, pack = _build(api, load_case, frozen_now, case_id)

    raw_by_local = {raw["case_local_id"]: raw for raw in case["items"]}
    assert pack.items, case_id
    for item in pack.items:
        local = item.evidence_id[len(run_spec.run_id) + 1:]
        raw = raw_by_local[local]
        assert item.evidence_id == _full_id(run_spec, local)
        assert item.source_uri == raw["source_uri"]
        assert item.fetched_at == datetimes(api, raw["fetched_at"])
        # date-only fixtures keep day precision; timestamp fixtures keep the instant
        assert item.published_at == datetimes(api, raw["published_at"])
        assert item.excerpt == raw["excerpt"]
        assert item.trust_label == raw["trust_label"]
        assert item.content_hash == raw["content_hash"]


def datetimes(api, raw_value):
    """Normalize a fixture timestamp exactly as the contract exposes it."""
    if isinstance(raw_value, str) and len(raw_value) == 10:
        return date.fromisoformat(raw_value)
    from datetime import datetime

    return datetime.fromisoformat(raw_value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Time filtering is wired into the pack API (representative slice)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def test_date_only_before_cutoff_admitted(pack_api, load_case, frozen_now):
    api = pack_api
    case, run_spec, pack = _build(api, load_case, frozen_now, "E-07")
    assert _admitted_local_ids(pack, run_spec) == case["expected"]["admitted"]
    # Day precision survives to the public form (no invented timestamp).
    assert isinstance(pack.items[0].published_at, date)
    assert not hasattr(pack.items[0].published_at, "hour")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "case_id, reason_name",
    [("E-16", "FUTURE_DATA"), ("E-17", "EVIDENCE_MISSING")],
)

"""Shared evidence-side contracts: ``RunSpec``, ``EvidenceItem``, ``EvidencePack``.

# Implements: FR-01, INV-02

Type-layer only. These models fix the SHAPE the evidence module (A) produces and
its consumers read; they do NOT filter by time, generate ids, dedupe, or compare
digests at pack time. Those behaviours belong to ``egta.evidence`` (A):

- ``evidence_id`` is generated by the evidence module from the run id + case local
  id; these types store the id they are given and never mint one.
- the UTC date filter (strictly-earlier admitted / same-date excluded / exact
  timestamp equality admitted) is A's; these types only carry its outcomes.
- ``content_hash`` is NOT cross-validated against ``excerpt`` here, so a tampered
  item is constructible; the evidence module recomputes and reports
  ``INTEGRITY_VIOLATION`` at pack time.

The shared ``ReasonCode`` is owned by the contracts package's events module; this
module imports it rather than defining a second enum.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator

from egta.contracts.events import ReasonCode

_HASH_PATTERN = r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
_DATE_ONLY = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")


class Availability(StrEnum):
    """Admission state of an evidence item.

    Distinct from ``ReasonCode``: ``availability`` is the state, ``reason_code`` is
    the cause. They are independent and neither substitutes for the other.
    """

    AVAILABLE = "available"
    STALE = "stale"
    UNREACHABLE = "unreachable"
    UNAVAILABLE = "unavailable"


def _normalize_time(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Normalize an evidence timestamp for ``published_at`` / ``fetched_at``.

    A bare ``YYYY-MM-DD`` is kept as a ``date`` so day precision survives to the
    public JSON form (no invented time or offset). Any other string is parsed as a
    datetime; a timezone-aware value is converted to UTC, and a naive one is kept
    as given. The contract frozen for these types does not require rejecting a naive
    evidence timestamp, so this function does not reject one here: deciding whether
    an evidence time is admissible (including a naive or malformed value) is A's
    ``egta.evidence`` time-policy responsibility, not this type's.
    """
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if _DATE_ONLY.fullmatch(value):
            return date.fromisoformat(value)
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        return parsed.astimezone(UTC) if parsed.tzinfo is not None else parsed
    if isinstance(value, datetime):
        return value.astimezone(UTC) if value.tzinfo is not None else value
    return value


class RunSpec(BaseModel):
    """Run definition shared by every module (plan §5.1).

    ``as_of`` is the analysis instant: a timezone-aware UTC datetime. A bare date
    or a naive timestamp is rejected (evidence may be date-only; ``as_of`` may not).
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)

    schema_version: str
    run_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    ticker: str = Field(min_length=1)
    as_of: datetime
    mode: str
    model_config_hash: str = Field(pattern=_HASH_PATTERN)
    prompt_hash: str = Field(pattern=_HASH_PATTERN)
    policy_hash: str = Field(pattern=_HASH_PATTERN)
    snapshot_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    limits: dict[str, Any]

    @field_validator("as_of", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _require_aware_instant(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        # Reject a bare date string outright: as_of must be an instant.
        if isinstance(value, str) and _DATE_ONLY.fullmatch(value):
            raise ValueError("as_of must be a timezone-aware datetime, not a bare date")
        return value

    @field_validator("as_of")
    @classmethod
    def _as_of_aware_utc(cls, value: datetime) -> datetime:
        if value.tzinfo is None or value.utcoffset() is None:
            raise ValueError("as_of must be timezone-aware (UTC)")
        return value.astimezone(UTC)


class EvidenceItem(BaseModel):
    """One admitted or excluded evidence item (plan §5.1).

    ``availability`` is required and enumerated. ``reason_code`` and
    ``conflict_group`` default to ``None``. ``published_at`` accepts a date-only
    value (kept as a date) or a full timestamp.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)

    evidence_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    source_uri: str = Field(min_length=1)
    published_at: date | datetime
    fetched_at: date | datetime
    content_hash: str = Field(pattern=_HASH_PATTERN)
    excerpt: str
    availability: Availability
    trust_label: str
    reason_code: ReasonCode | None = None
    conflict_group: str | None = None

    @field_validator("published_at", "fetched_at", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _keep_day_precision(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        return _normalize_time(value)


class ExcludedItem(BaseModel):
    """A pack exclusion: exactly the three agreed fields.

    Not an ``EvidenceItem``: no ``published_at`` and no full ``evidence_id``.
    ``case_local_id == "provider"`` marks a provider-level failure. Provider error
    detail is recorded by the evidence module in the audit payload, not here.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    case_local_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    availability: Availability
    reason_code: ReasonCode


class EvidencePack(BaseModel):
    """The evidence module's output for one run (plan §5.1).

    ``excluded_items`` is required (an explicit empty list is valid; omitting it
    fails). ``cutoff`` is the same instant as the run/fixture ``as_of``.
    ``pack_hash`` is carried as supplied; its algorithm is not frozen here.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)

    run_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    snapshot_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    items: list[EvidenceItem]
    excluded_items: list[ExcludedItem]
    cutoff: datetime
    pack_hash: str = Field(pattern=_HASH_PATTERN)

    @field_validator("cutoff")
    @classmethod
    def _cutoff_aware_utc(cls, value: datetime) -> datetime:
        if value.tzinfo is None or value.utcoffset() is None:
            raise ValueError("cutoff must be timezone-aware (UTC)")
        return value.astimezone(UTC)

"""Pack-level evidence assembly for FR-01 / INV-02 (module A).

``build_pack`` turns raw provider items into an immutable :class:`EvidencePack`
and its :class:`~egta.contracts.ExcludedItem` list; ``validate_claims`` fails
closed on a claim that cites an evidence id the pack does not contain.

# Implements: FR-01 (evidence pack), INV-02 (point-in-time admissibility)

Design decisions frozen by the approved pack-level spec
(``test/offline/evidence/test_pack.py``, PR #25) and its trace:

* ``pack_hash`` is **computed here**, never supplied by a caller. It is the SHA-256
  of the canonical ``evidence_fields(pack)`` and therefore equals
  :func:`egta.risk_gate.canonical.recompute_evidence_hash`; the risk gate recomputes
  and rejects any mismatch as ``INTEGRITY_VIOLATION`` (``test_pack_hash_matches_risk_gate_canonical``).
* Claim citations use the **full** evidence id ``<run_id>-<case_local_id>``, matching
  the risk gate's index (``risk_gate/rules.py`` ``_check_claims``).
* A dangling citation raises :class:`InvalidCitation` carrying
  ``ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION`` and naming the bad id.
* ``source_type == "cache"`` is always stale (``STALE_DATA`` / ``stale``); there is
  no age-based freshness threshold in this spec.
* ``pack.items`` preserves raw input order (admitted items only). A duplicate
  (same ``source_uri`` + publication instant + ``content_hash``) is silently
  collapsed, not listed as an exclusion.
* A caller-supplied ``conflict_key`` groups *more than one* admitted item; a single
  admitted item is never grouped.

Pure time filtering (E-13..E-20, E-27, E-28, E-31) is owned by
:func:`egta.evidence.time_policy.is_admissible`; this module only wires its verdicts
into the pack.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
from typing import Any

from egta.contracts import Availability, EvidenceItem, EvidencePack, ExcludedItem, RunSpec
from egta.contracts.events import ReasonCode
from egta.evidence.time_policy import is_admissible
from egta.risk_gate.canonical import recompute_evidence_hash

_TIME_GRANULARITY_NONE = "none"
_INTEGRITY_AVAILABILITY = Availability.UNAVAILABLE
_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ID = "provider"
_HASH_ZERO = "0" * 64


class InvalidCitation(Exception):
    """A claim cites an evidence id absent from the pack (``INVALID_CITATION``).

    Carries the offending id so callers can report precisely which citation was
    dangling without re-parsing the message.
    """

    def __init__(self, evidence_id: str) -> None:
        self.evidence_id = evidence_id
        self.reason_code = ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION
        super().__init__(
            f"{ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION.value}: claim cites unknown evidence id "
            f"{evidence_id!r}"
        )


def _sha256_hex(text: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _publication_instant(published_at: Any) -> Any:
    """Normalize ``published_at`` for dedupe keys only (never mutates the item).

    Date-only values collapse to their ``date``; aware datetimes to UTC; naive and
    malformed values are kept verbatim so distinct bad values stay distinct.
    """
    if isinstance(published_at, datetime):
        return published_at.astimezone(UTC) if published_at.tzinfo is not None else published_at
    if isinstance(published_at, date):
        return published_at
    if isinstance(published_at, str):
        try:
            parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(published_at.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        except ValueError:
            return published_at
        return parsed.astimezone(UTC) if parsed.tzinfo is not None else parsed
    return published_at


def _raw_get(raw: Mapping[str, Any], key: str) -> Any:
    return raw.get(key)


def _is_cache(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    return _raw_get(raw, "source_type") == "cache"


def _is_tampered(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    excerpt = _raw_get(raw, "excerpt")
    content_hash = _raw_get(raw, "content_hash")
    if not isinstance(excerpt, str) or not isinstance(content_hash, str):
        return False
    return _sha256_hex(excerpt) != content_hash


def _dedupe_key(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Any, Any, Any]:
    return (
        _raw_get(raw, "source_uri"),
        _publication_instant(_raw_get(raw, "published_at")),
        _raw_get(raw, "content_hash"),
    )


def _excluded(case_local_id: str, reason: ReasonCode, availability: Availability) -> ExcludedItem:
    return ExcludedItem(
        case_local_id=case_local_id,
        availability=availability,
        reason_code=reason,
    )


def _to_evidence_item(
    run_id: str,
    raw: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    conflict_group: str | None,
) -> EvidenceItem:
    return EvidenceItem(
        evidence_id=f"{run_id}-{raw['case_local_id']}",
        source_uri=raw["source_uri"],
        published_at=raw["published_at"],
        fetched_at=raw["fetched_at"],
        content_hash=raw["content_hash"],
        excerpt=raw["excerpt"],
        availability=Availability.AVAILABLE,
        trust_label=raw["trust_label"],
        reason_code=None,
        conflict_group=conflict_group,
    )


def _time_verdict(raw: Mapping[str, Any], run_spec: RunSpec):
    granularity = _raw_get(raw, "time_granularity", _TIME_GRANULARITY_NONE)
    return is_admissible(
        published_at=_raw_get(raw, "published_at"),
        time_granularity=granularity if isinstance(granularity, str) else _TIME_GRANULARITY_NONE,
        as_of=run_spec.as_of,
    )


def _assemble(
    run_spec: RunSpec,
    raw_items: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]],
    *,
    provider_error: Any,
    conflict_key: str | None,
) -> tuple[list[EvidenceItem], list[ExcludedItem]]:
    exclusions: list[ExcludedItem] = []

    if provider_error is not None:
        exclusions.append(
            _excluded(_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ID, ReasonCode.VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE, Availability.UNREACHABLE)
        )

    admitted_raw: list[Mapping[str, Any]] = []
    seen: set[tuple[Any, Any, Any]] = set()

    for raw in raw_items:
        local_id = _raw_get(raw, "case_local_id")
        if _is_cache(raw):
            exclusions.append(_excluded(local_id, ReasonCode.STALE_DATA, Availability.STALE))
            continue
        if _is_tampered(raw):
            exclusions.append(
                _excluded(local_id, ReasonCode.INTEGRITY_VIOLATION, _INTEGRITY_AVAILABILITY)
            )
            continue
        verdict = _time_verdict(raw, run_spec)
        if not verdict.admissible:
            exclusions.append(
                _excluded(local_id, ReasonCode(verdict.reason_code), Availability.UNAVAILABLE)
            )
            continue
        key = _dedupe_key(raw)
        if key in seen:
            # Silent collapse: a duplicate is neither admitted nor an exclusion.
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        admitted_raw.append(raw)

    group = conflict_key if (conflict_key is not None and len(admitted_raw) > 1) else None
    items = [
        _to_evidence_item(run_spec.run_id, raw, conflict_group=group) for raw in admitted_raw
    ]
    return items, exclusions


def _pack_with_hash(
    run_spec: RunSpec,
    items: list[EvidenceItem],
    exclusions: list[ExcludedItem],
) -> EvidencePack:
    # Build with a placeholder, then bind pack_hash to the canonical recomputation
    # over the pack's evidence_fields. recompute_evidence_hash ignores pack_hash, so
    # the placeholder never affects the digest.
    provisional = EvidencePack(
        run_id=run_spec.run_id,
        snapshot_id=run_spec.snapshot_id,
        items=items,
        excluded_items=exclusions,
        cutoff=run_spec.as_of,
        pack_hash=_HASH_ZERO,
    )
    pack_hash = recompute_evidence_hash(provisional)
    return provisional.model_copy(update={"pack_hash": pack_hash})


def build_pack(
    run_spec: RunSpec,
    raw_items: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]],
    *,
    provider_error: Any = None,
    conflict_key: str | None = None,
) -> EvidencePack:
    """Assemble an :class:`EvidencePack` from raw provider items (FR-01 / INV-02).

    ``provider_error`` (any non-``None`` value) records a single provider-level
    exclusion (``VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE`` / ``unreachable``). ``conflict_key`` marks a
    caller-known conflict group across all admitted items when more than one
    remains after filtering/dedupe.
    """
    items, exclusions = _assemble(
        run_spec,
        raw_items,
        provider_error=provider_error,
        conflict_key=conflict_key,
    )
    return _pack_with_hash(run_spec, items, exclusions)


def _claim_evidence_ids(claim: Any) -> Iterable[str]:
    if isinstance(claim, Mapping):
        return claim.get("evidence_ids", ()) or ()
    return getattr(claim, "evidence_ids", ()) or ()


def validate_claims(pack: EvidencePack, claims: Iterable[Any]) -> None:
    """Fail closed if any claim cites an evidence id absent from ``pack``.

    Raises :class:`InvalidCitation` naming the first dangling id. Accepts claim
    mappings or objects exposing ``evidence_ids`` (full ``<run_id>-<case_local_id>``
    ids, matching the risk gate's index).
    """
    known = {item.evidence_id for item in pack.items}
    for claim in claims:
        for evidence_id in _claim_evidence_ids(claim):
            if evidence_id not in known:
                raise InvalidCitation(str(evidence_id))


__all__ = ["InvalidCitation", "build_pack", "validate_claims"]

---BODY---
## Requirement and scope

Test-first spec PR (GATE-01) for **FR-01 EvidencePack** behaviour and **INV-02** (time filtering wired into the pack API). Rebased onto post-#21 main.

- Requirement IDs: FR-01, INV-02 (and NFR-10 via date-only precision carried through).
- `test/offline/evidence/test_pack.py`: **20 test functions / 33 cases**, `pytestmark = pytest.mark.spec`.
- `docs/req/trace-FR-01-pack.md`, `docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-01-pack.txt`, `docs/evidence/FR-01/pack-red-baseline.txt` updated.
- No fixture changes, no `src/` changes, no implementation code.

## Expected RED (post-#21)

B #21 is merged to `main` (`141547a`), so `egta.contracts` already exports `RunSpec/EvidenceItem/EvidencePack/ExcludedItem/Availability`. The RED is now purely the missing evidence implementation:

- `pytest -o addopts="--strict-markers" -m spec test/offline/evidence -q` -> **33 errors**, `ImportError: cannot import name 'InvalidCitation' from 'egta.evidence'` (not a contracts gap). Full capture in `docs/evidence/FR-01/pack-red-baseline.txt`.
- `pytest test/offline/evidence -m "not spec" -q` -> 13 passed, 33 deselected.
- Default suite untouched: `pytest` (testpaths=tests) -> 1412 passed, 1 skipped.

## pack_hash A→D alignment (resolved, not just claimed)

`test_pack_hash_matches_risk_gate_canonical` asserts

```
pack.pack_hash == egta.risk_gate.canonical.recompute_evidence_hash(pack)
```

over E-01/E-07/E-22/E-23, using the canonical helper **already on main** (`src/egta/risk_gate/canonical.py`, used by `rules.py`). This is a real cross-module integration check — an implementation whose `build_pack` produces any other digest will fail it (and would otherwise be rejected as `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` by the risk gate). No ADR-004 is invented; the executable equality is the frozen contract, and the trace says so.

## Fixture -> assertion map

| Group | Fixtures | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| normal admit | E-01..E-06, E-08..E-10, E-12 | ids/order, `excluded_items == []`, `cutoff == as_of`, admitted `reason_code is None`, `availability == AVAILABLE` |
| field mapping | E-01, E-07, E-10 | raw -> EvidenceItem source_uri/published_at/fetched_at/excerpt/trust_label/content_hash |
| time wired in | E-07, E-16, E-17 | E-07 date-only admitted (day precision); E-16 FUTURE_DATA / E-17 EVIDENCE_MISSING |
| dedupe | E-21 | only `E-21-1` admitted; `E-21-2` neither admitted nor excluded |
| conflict | E-22 | both retained; group == caller-supplied `conflict_key` |
| integrity | E-23, E-30 | tampered copy excluded INTEGRITY_VIOLATION; E-23 keeps original |
| provider failure | E-24, E-25 | `items == []`; provider exclusion VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE/unreachable |
| stale cache | E-26 (+ fresh non-cache control) | cache item STALE_DATA/stale, never available |
| citation | E-29 | pack builds; `validate_claims` raises `InvalidCitation` naming the bad full id; valid id passes |
| pack_hash | E-01 (+ E-07/E-22/E-23 for A→D) | 64-hex, deterministic, content-bound, **== risk_gate canonical** |

## Test-approval evidence

- `test_content_commit`: `cd0cb0c`, `actual_cases: 33`; record `docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-01-pack.txt` (per-file/aggregate + reviewed head PENDING).
- Implementation PR must descend from this spec's merge commit and provide `egta.evidence.InvalidCitation` + `build_pack`/`validate_claims`.
- D is code owner of `test/offline/evidence/`; approval required per GATE-01. Do not self-merge.

## Verification

- `ruff check .` -> All checks passed.
- `py_compile test/offline/evidence/test_pack.py` -> exit 0.
- 20 functions / 33 cases collected; `git diff --check` clean.

## Merge and recovery

- Rebased onto `main 141547a` (B #21 in). No runtime effect (spec-only); default suite unaffected.
- Revert = drop the commits.

cd /home/lenovo/projects/EGTA-CS5351-Group20 && cat > /tmp/pr_impl_body.md <<'EOF'
## Requirement and scope

Implementation (GATE-01 descendant) of module A's **FR-01 EvidencePack** and **INV-02** wiring.

- Requirement IDs: FR-01, INV-02, NFR-10.
- Files: `src/egta/evidence/pack.py` (new), `src/egta/evidence/__init__.py` (exports), `docs/evidence/FR-01/pack-impl-green.txt`, `docs/ai-use-log-A-fragment.yaml`.
- No changes to the frozen spec (`test/offline/evidence/test_pack.py`), contracts, or any other module.

## Approved-test evidence (GATE-01)

- Spec PR: **#25** (merged as `f9ca5d1`), approved by D.
- This branch is created directly off `f9ca5d1`; first implementation commit is `0a8bc9a` (descends from the spec merge).
- Frozen test untouched: `test_pack.py` SHA-256 `75fc9dc5bbdf6a69fcc439a7f2c0a71ea2b01c7bf15e5c1567ed9fa574aaecac` (matches `docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-01-pack.txt`).
- RED -> green: `pytest -m spec test/offline/evidence` was **33 errors** on the spec branch; now **33 passed**.

## What it implements (per frozen #25 decisions)

- `build_pack(run_spec, raw_items, *, provider_error=None, conflict_key=None) -> EvidencePack`: admission, raw->EvidenceItem field mapping, dedupe by (source_uri, published_at, content_hash), caller-supplied `conflict_key` grouping for >1 admitted item, integrity via `sha256(excerpt) != content_hash`, provider-level exclusion (`VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE`/`unreachable`), cache-always-stale (`STALE_DATA`/`stale`), INV-02 time filtering via `time_policy.is_admissible`.
- `validate_claims(pack, claims)`: full `<run_id>-<case_local_id>` ids; dangling cite raises `InvalidCitation` (`ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION`) naming the bad id.
- `pack_hash` is **computed by `build_pack`** via `egta.risk_gate.canonical.recompute_evidence_hash`, so the risk gate cannot reject the pack as `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` (this is the A->D equality test `test_pack_hash_matches_risk_gate_canonical`).

## Verification and governance

- `pytest -o addopts=--strict-markers -m spec test/offline/evidence -q` -> **33 passed**, 13 deselected.
- `pytest -o addopts=--strict-markers -m "not spec" test/offline/evidence -q` -> 13 passed (INV-02 no regression).
- `pytest -o addopts=--strict-markers test/offline/risk_gate -q` -> **139 passed** (A->D consume still green).
- `ruff check src/egta/evidence test/offline/evidence` -> clean; `mypy src/egta/evidence` -> no issues.
- Evidence: `docs/evidence/FR-01/pack-impl-green.txt`.
- AI-use log (GATE-06): `docs/ai-use-log-A-fragment.yaml` session `ses_feat_FR01_evidence_pack_impl`.

## Merge and recovery

- No runtime effect on the existing default suite (spec only selected by `-m spec`).
- Revert = drop commit `0a8bc9a`; no data/state migration.
- Reviewer: D is code owner of `test/offline/evidence/`; independent approval required. Do not self-merge.
EOF

Index: .github/workflows/ci.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/ci.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/ci.yml	
@@ -1,255 +1,257 @@
 name: CI
 
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main, 'v*']
   pull_request:
 
 concurrency:
   group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
   cancel-in-progress: true
 
 jobs:
   test:
     name: tests (py${{ matrix.python-version }}${{ matrix.tz && format(', {0}', matrix.tz) || '' }})
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     # Experimental interpreters (e.g. 3.14) are non-blocking.
     continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}
     strategy:
       fail-fast: false
       matrix:
         python-version: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
         experimental: [false]
         # One run away from UTC, so a test that only passes in UTC fails here.
         # 3.14 is include-only and experimental (truly non-blocking) to avoid
         # false reds from a failing pip install / provider wheel gap.
         include:
           - python-version: "3.14"
             experimental: true
           - python-version: "3.12"
             tz: America/New_York
             experimental: false
     env:
       TZ: ${{ matrix.tz }}
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
       - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
         with:
           python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
       - name: Install (with dev extras)
         run: |
           python -m pip install --upgrade pip
           pip install -e ".[dev]"
       - name: Run test suite
         run: pytest -q
 
   smoke-install:
     name: clean-install smoke
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
       - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
         with:
           python-version: "3.12"
       - name: Fresh install (no dev extras) and import
         run: |
           python -m pip install --upgrade pip
           pip install .
           # Catches undeclared runtime deps (e.g. #994 python-dotenv): a bare
           # install must import the package and the CLI module.
           python -c "import tradingagents, cli.main; print('clean-install import OK')"
 
   lint:
     name: ruff (strict, full repo)
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
       - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
         with:
           python-version: "3.12"
       - name: Install ruff
         run: pip install "ruff>=0.16"
       - name: Lint the repository
         # The repo is fully clean under the strict select, so we lint everything
         # (generated results/ is excluded via pyproject extend-exclude).
         run: ruff check .
 
   # Offline spec suites, gated per-suite (A review: Block 1 + Block 2).
   #
   # Each suite independently detects its module directory so one unimplemented
   # module never reds another:
   #   contracts  ⇔ src/egta/contracts   (7 explicit FR-05 files; count read from
   #                docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-05-contracts.txt actual_cases, NOT
   #                hardcoded 199; not the whole directory -m spec, so other specs
   #                such as FR-01 evidence cannot contaminate it)
   #   evaluation ⇔ src/egta/evaluation  (-m spec test/offline/evaluation, 28)
   #   risk_gate  ⇔ src/egta/risk_gate   (test/offline/risk_gate by path, 139)
   #   budget     ⇔ src/egta/budget      (-m spec test/offline/budget; count read
   #                from docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-02-budget.txt actual_cases;
   #                N/A until FR-02 is implemented + its record exists)
   # If a suite's dir is absent it reports ::notice:: N/A (skip only that suite).
   #
   # The gate runs pytest (not just --collect-only): the run's terminal summary
   # `passed` count must equal the expected number, and any skip/xfail/xpass/error
   # fails the gate. --collect-only is also checked for an extra consistency guard.
   #
   # GATE-06 (AI-use log) — why there is no status check here (D item 4): GATE-06 is
   # a *review-time* rule, not a deterministic build artifact. A reliable CI check
   # would need to know, per PR, whether a code/test/prompt file changed AND whether
   # docs/ai-use-log.yaml changed in the SAME PR — but docs-only / CI-only / governance
   # PRs legitimately change no code and add no log entry, so a naive "require an
   # ai-use-log diff" check would false-fail them. GATE-06 is therefore enforced by
   # the human reviewer (D/A) on the PR, not by a required status check. If the team
   # later decides to automate it, it must be a diff-aware job (only fire when code/
   # test/prompt paths changed) — tracked as a follow-up, not enabled here.
   offline-tests:
     name: offline spec suites (per-suite gate)
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
       - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
         with:
           python-version: "3.12"
       - name: Install (with dev extras)
         run: |
           python -m pip install --upgrade pip
           pip install -e ".[dev]"
       - name: Gate each offline suite
         env:
           # contracts + budget expected are read from their approval records (F1
           # scheme 2) so a spec PR and CI can never drift. E2/risk_gate use env.
           CONTRACTS_RECORD: "docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-05-contracts.txt"
           BUDGET_RECORD: "docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-02-budget.txt"
           EXPECT_EVALUATION: "28"
           EXPECT_RISK_GATE: "139"  # A confirmed FR-04 126 + 13 = 139
+          EXPECT_EVIDENCE: "37"  # FR-01 pack: 33 frozen spec cases + 4 precedence cases
         run: |
           python - <<'PY'
           import os
           import re
           import subprocess
           import sys
           from pathlib import Path
 
           # FR-05 contracts share test/offline/contracts with OTHER specs (e.g.
           # FR-01 test_evidence_contracts.py lands there via #5), so we list
           # FR-05's files explicitly to keep its actual_cases uncontaminated.
-          # NOTE: FR-01 evidence is NOT gated here yet — it needs #5 merged + B's
-          # EvidenceItem/EvidencePack types + an actual_cases record. Tracked as a
-          # follow-up debt (owner E, verifier A), not a suite in this job.
+          # FR-01 evidence is gated as its own suite below (by path, so it cannot
+          # contaminate the contracts suite and vice versa): 37 = 33 frozen pack
+          # cases (#25) + 4 classification-precedence cases (test_pack_precedence.py).
           _CONTRACTS_DIR = "test/offline/contracts"
           _FR05_FILES = [
               "_crash_child.py",  # not selected; harmless if absent
               "test_comparison.py", "test_events.py", "test_audit.py",
               "test_replay.py", "test_evaluation_result.py", "test_manifest.py",
               "test_metrics_serialization.py",
           ]
           _fr05_paths = [f"{_CONTRACTS_DIR}/{n}" for n in _FR05_FILES
                          if n.startswith("test_")]
 
           # (suite-name, module-dir, pytest-args, expected-source)
           #   expected-source: None => read contracts record;
           #                    "ENV:NAME" => env var; "RECORD:path" => approval record
           suites = [
               ("contracts",  "src/egta/contracts",  ["-m", "spec", *_fr05_paths], None),
               ("evaluation", "src/egta/evaluation", ["-m", "spec", "test/offline/evaluation"], "ENV:EXPECT_EVALUATION"),
               ("risk_gate",  "src/egta/risk_gate",  ["test/offline/risk_gate"],                "ENV:EXPECT_RISK_GATE"),
+              ("evidence",   "src/egta/evidence",   ["-m", "spec", "test/offline/evidence"],    "ENV:EXPECT_EVIDENCE"),
               ("budget",     "src/egta/budget",     ["-m", "spec", "test/offline/budget"],      "RECORD:docs/approvals/test-hash-FR-02-budget.txt"),
           ]
 
           # pytest terminal summary, e.g. "123 passed, 2 skipped in 0.4s".
           _SUMMARY = re.compile(
               r"(\d+)\s+passed|(\d+)\s+failed|(\d+)\s+error|(\d+)\s+skipped"
               r"|(\d+)\s+xfailed|(\d+)\s+xpassed"
           )
 
           def run_pytest(args):
               return subprocess.run(
                   [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-o", "addopts=--strict-markers",
                    "-q", "-rsx", *args],
                   capture_output=True, text=True,
               )
 
           def collect_count(args):
               out = subprocess.run(
                   [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-o", "addopts=--strict-markers",
                    "--collect-only", "-q", *args],
                   capture_output=True, text=True,
               )
               if out.returncode != 0:
                   return None
               ids = {
                   line.strip() for line in out.stdout.splitlines()
                   if "::" in line and not line.strip().startswith(("<", "=", "collected", "no tests"))
               }
               return len(ids)
 
           def summary_passed(text):
               # Take the LAST line that looks like the terminal summary.
               counts = {}
               for line in reversed(text.splitlines()):
                   if "passed" in line or "failed" in line or "error" in line or "skipped" in line:
                       for m in _SUMMARY.finditer(line):
                           if m.group(1) is not None: counts["passed"] = int(m.group(1))
                           elif m.group(2) is not None: counts["failed"] = int(m.group(2))
                           elif m.group(3) is not None: counts["error"] = int(m.group(3))
                           elif m.group(4) is not None: counts["skipped"] = int(m.group(4))
                           elif m.group(5) is not None: counts["xfailed"] = int(m.group(5))
                           elif m.group(6) is not None: counts["xpassed"] = int(m.group(6))
                       if counts:
                           return counts
               return counts
 
           def expected_from_record(path):
               # F1 scheme 2: parse `actual_cases: <n>` from the approval record.
               if not Path(path).is_file():
                   return None
               text = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
               m = re.search(r"^\s*actual_cases:\s*(\d+)", text, re.MULTILINE)
               if not m:
                   return None
               return int(m.group(1))
 
           failures = []
           for name, moddir, args, env in suites:
               if not Path(moddir).is_dir():
                   print(f"::notice::{name}: {moddir} absent -- N/A (suite skipped, not pass/fail)")
                   continue
               if env is None:
                   expected = expected_from_record(os.environ["CONTRACTS_RECORD"])
               elif env.startswith("RECORD:"):
                   expected = expected_from_record(env.split(":", 1)[1])
               elif env.startswith("ENV:"):
                   expected = int(os.environ[env.split(":", 1)[1]])
               else:
                   expected = int(os.environ[env])
               if expected is None:
                   # Directory exists but no approval record yet -> N/A (not a fail).
                   print(f"::notice::{name}: no expected count record -- N/A (suite skipped)")
                   continue
 
               # 1) collect-only consistency (extra guard; not the sole gate).
               collected = collect_count(args)
               print(f"{name}: collect-only={collected} expected={expected}")
 
               # 2) REAL run; terminal summary must show exactly `expected` passed.
               res = run_pytest(args)
               sys.stdout.write(res.stdout)
               sys.stderr.write(res.stderr)
               counts = summary_passed(res.stdout)
               passed = counts.get("passed", 0)
               bad = {k: counts.get(k, 0) for k in ("failed", "error", "skipped", "xfailed", "xpassed")}
               bad = {k: v for k, v in bad.items() if v}
 
               ok = (res.returncode == 0 and passed == expected and not bad
                     and (collected is None or collected == expected))
               status = "OK" if ok else "FAIL"
               print(f"{name}: passed={passed} expected={expected} bad={bad} rc={res.returncode} -> {status}")
               if not ok:
                   failures.append(name)
                   print(f"::error::{name}: expected exactly {expected} passed, no skip/xfail/"
                         f"error; got passed={passed} bad={bad} rc={res.returncode}")
 
           if failures:
               raise SystemExit(f"offline gate failed: {', '.join(failures)}")
           print("All applicable offline suites passed at their exact expected counts.")
           PY

+# Trace — FR-01 evidence pack implementation (A) + classification precedence
+
+Implementation-side trace for the FR-01 `build_pack` / `validate_claims`
+implementation (PR for `src/egta/evidence/pack.py`). The **frozen** pack spec and
+its trace live in `test/offline/evidence/test_pack.py` and
+`docs/req/trace-FR-01-pack.md` (PR #25, merged `f9ca5d1`); this file does not
+modify them. It documents the implementation boundary and the additive
+classification-precedence tests `test/offline/evidence/test_pack_precedence.py`.
+
+## Frozen spec vs. additive cases
+
+| Suite | File | Cases | Status |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Frozen pack spec (#25) | `test_pack.py` | 33 | approved by D; hash `75fc9dc5…`, unchanged |
+| Classification precedence (this PR) | `test_pack_precedence.py` | 4 | additive; selected by `-m spec` |
+
+Total FR-01 evidence spec cases = **37** (CI `EXPECT_EVIDENCE=37`).
+
+## Classification precedence (resolves D's audit-precedence question)
+
+`_assemble` classifies each raw item in this order, first match wins:
+
+1. **integrity** — `sha256(excerpt) != content_hash` → `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION`
+   (availability `unavailable`). Runs *before* the cache check, so a **tampered
+   cache item** is reported as tampering, not silently downgraded to stale. This
+   is the FR-01/T04 audit-correct choice.
+2. **staleness** — well-formed `source_type == "cache"` → `STALE_DATA`
+   (availability `stale`). Frozen E-26 rule; no age threshold.
+3. **time** — INV-02 admissibility via `egta.evidence.time_policy.is_admissible`
+   (`FUTURE_DATA` / `EVIDENCE_MISSING` / `INVALID_TIME`).
+4. **dedupe** — collapse identical `(source_uri, publication instant, content_hash)`;
+   a duplicate is neither admitted nor excluded.
+
+Consequences pinned by tests:
+
+| Test | Input | Expected |
+|---|---|---|
+| `test_tampered_cache_is_integrity_not_stale` | cache item, `sha256(excerpt) != content_hash` | `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` / `unavailable` |
+| `test_well_formed_cache_still_stale` | clean cache item (control) | `STALE_DATA` / `stale` (E-26 unchanged) |
+| `test_future_cache_is_stale_not_future_data` | cache item, `published_at` after `as_of` | `STALE_DATA` / `stale` (cache staged before time filter) |
+| `test_future_non_cache_is_future_data` | non-cache item, future (E-16) | `FUTURE_DATA` / `unavailable` |
+
+## Cross-module import boundary (NFR-06 / AGENTS.md §3)
+
+`build_pack` needs the *same* canonical hash the risk gate recomputes, or the
+pack is rejected as `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION`. Importing `egta.risk_gate.canonical`
+from `egta.evidence` would be a forbidden cross-module import. Fix:
+
+- The canonical helpers moved to `egta.contracts.canonical` (shared, dependency-free,
+  operates on contract types). Both business modules now import it from
+  `egta.contracts`, which is the only cross-module dependency a module may have.
+- `egta/risk_gate/canonical.py` is kept as a thin re-export shim so existing
+  importers (`test/offline/risk_gate/test_evidence_time_policy.py`, D's gate code)
+  keep working.
+- `egta.evidence.pack` imports only `egta.contracts*` and its own module.
+
+This is a shared-contracts change (B-owned); it must be reviewed by the contracts
+custodian in addition to D. No algorithm change — the canonical form and
+`recompute_evidence_hash` output are byte-identical (risk_gate 139 tests and
+contracts 288 tests still pass).
+
+## Verification
+
+- evidence spec: `pytest -m spec test/offline/evidence` → 37 passed.
+- evidence not-spec: `pytest -m "not spec" test/offline/evidence` → 13 passed (INV-02).
+- risk_gate: `pytest test/offline/risk_gate` → 139 passed (A→D equality intact).
+- contracts: `pytest -m spec test/offline/contracts` → 288 passed.
+- CI offline gate (local simulation of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`): evidence
+  `passed=37 expected=37 -> OK`; all suites OK; exit 0.
+- ruff clean; mypy clean.

--- src/egta/contracts/canonical.py

@@ -0,0 +1,188 @@
+"""Canonical JSON and SHA-256 helpers shared across modules.
+
+Relocated here from ``egta.risk_gate.canonical`` so that the canonical form is a
+*contract-level* concern: both the risk gate (D) and the evidence pack (A) must
+produce byte-identical hashes for ``evidence_hash`` / ``proposal_hash`` /
+``policy_hash``. Importing this from ``egta.contracts`` keeps every business
+module within the allowed "contracts + own module" import boundary (AGENTS.md
+§3, NFR-06) instead of depending on another business module's private code.
+
+The canonical form: sorted object keys, compact separators, UTF-8, Decimal as a
+fixed-point string, aware datetimes normalized to UTC, date-only values as ISO
+date strings, tuples as arrays, and SHA-256 lowercase hex.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
+from decimal import Decimal
+from typing import Any
+
+_HASH_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
+
+
+def hash_is_valid(value: Any) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(value, str) and _HASH_PATTERN.fullmatch(value) is not None
+
+
+def _normalize(value: Any) -> Any:
+    if value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, str)):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, Decimal):
+        return format(value, "f")
+    if isinstance(value, datetime):
+        if value.tzinfo is None or value.utcoffset() is None:
+            return value.isoformat()
+        return value.astimezone(UTC).isoformat()
+    if isinstance(value, date):
+        return value.isoformat()
+    if isinstance(value, int):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, float):
+        return repr(value)
+    if isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
+        return [_normalize(item) for item in value]
+    if isinstance(value, (set, frozenset)):
+        return sorted(_normalize(item) for item in value)
+    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
+        items = sorted(value.items(), key=lambda pair: str(pair[0]))
+        return {str(key): _normalize(item) for key, item in items}
+    if hasattr(value, "to_canonical_dict"):
+        return _normalize(value.to_canonical_dict())
+    raise TypeError(f"cannot canonicalize {type(value)!r}")
+
+
+def canonical_bytes(value: Any) -> bytes:
+    return json.dumps(
+        _normalize(value),
+        sort_keys=True,
+        separators=(",", ":"),
+        ensure_ascii=False,
+        allow_nan=False,
+    ).encode("utf-8")
+
+
+def sha256_hex(value: Any) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(value)).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _claim_dict(claim: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if isinstance(claim, Mapping):
+        return {
+            "claim_id": claim.get("claim_id"),
+            "text": claim.get("text"),
+            "evidence_ids": claim.get("evidence_ids", ()),
+            "stance": claim.get("stance"),
+            "counterargument": claim.get("counterargument"),
+            "unresolved": claim.get("unresolved"),
+        }
+    return {
+        "claim_id": getattr(claim, "claim_id", None),
+        "text": getattr(claim, "text", None),
+        "evidence_ids": getattr(claim, "evidence_ids", ()),
+        "stance": getattr(claim, "stance", None),
+        "counterargument": getattr(claim, "counterargument", None),
+        "unresolved": getattr(claim, "unresolved", None),
+    }
+
+
+def _item_dict(item: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if isinstance(item, Mapping):
+        return {
+            "evidence_id": item.get("evidence_id"),
+            "source_uri": item.get("source_uri"),
+            "published_at": item.get("published_at"),
+            "fetched_at": item.get("fetched_at"),
+            "content_hash": item.get("content_hash"),
+            "excerpt": item.get("excerpt"),
+            "availability": item.get("availability"),
+            "trust_label": item.get("trust_label"),
+        }
+    return {
+        "evidence_id": getattr(item, "evidence_id", None),
+        "source_uri": getattr(item, "source_uri", None),
+        "published_at": getattr(item, "published_at", None),
+        "fetched_at": getattr(item, "fetched_at", None),
+        "content_hash": getattr(item, "content_hash", None),
+        "excerpt": getattr(item, "excerpt", None),
+        "availability": getattr(item, "availability", None),
+        "trust_label": getattr(item, "trust_label", None),
+    }
+
+
+def proposal_fields(proposal: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    claims = getattr(proposal, "claims", ()) or ()
+    return {
+        "proposal_id": getattr(proposal, "proposal_id", None),
+        "run_id": getattr(proposal, "run_id", None),
+        "ticker": getattr(proposal, "ticker", None),
+        "action": getattr(proposal, "action", None),
+        "quantity": getattr(proposal, "quantity", None),
+        "currency": getattr(proposal, "currency", None),
+        "reference_price": getattr(proposal, "reference_price", None),
+        "price_time": getattr(proposal, "price_time", None),
+        "claims": tuple(_claim_dict(claim) for claim in claims),
+        "evidence_pack_hash": getattr(proposal, "evidence_pack_hash", None),
+        "portfolio_version": getattr(proposal, "portfolio_version", None),
+        "policy_hash": getattr(proposal, "policy_hash", None),
+        "expires_at": getattr(proposal, "expires_at", None),
+    }
+
+
+def policy_fields(policy: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "version": getattr(policy, "version", None),
+        "base_currency": getattr(policy, "base_currency", None),
+        "max_position_pct": getattr(policy, "max_position_pct", None),
+        "max_order_pct": getattr(policy, "max_order_pct", None),
+        "price_freshness_seconds": getattr(policy, "price_freshness_seconds", None),
+        "fee_bps": getattr(policy, "fee_bps", None),
+        "slippage_bps": getattr(policy, "slippage_bps", None),
+        "allowed_actions": getattr(policy, "allowed_actions", frozenset()),
+        "long_only": getattr(policy, "long_only", None),
+        "paper_only": getattr(policy, "paper_only", None),
+        "effective_from": getattr(policy, "effective_from", None),
+        "expires_at": getattr(policy, "expires_at", None),
+        "quantization": getattr(policy, "quantization", None),
+    }
+
+
+def evidence_fields(pack: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    items = getattr(pack, "items", ()) or ()
+    excluded = getattr(pack, "excluded_items", ()) or ()
+    return {
+        "run_id": getattr(pack, "run_id", None),
+        "snapshot_id": getattr(pack, "snapshot_id", None),
+        "items": tuple(_item_dict(item) for item in items),
+        "excluded_items": tuple(_item_dict(item) for item in excluded),
+        "cutoff": getattr(pack, "cutoff", None),
+    }
+
+
+def recompute_proposal_hash(proposal: Any) -> str:
+    return sha256_hex(proposal_fields(proposal))
+
+
+def recompute_policy_hash(policy: Any) -> str:
+    return sha256_hex(policy_fields(policy))
+
+
+def recompute_evidence_hash(pack: Any) -> str:
+    return sha256_hex(evidence_fields(pack))
+
+
+def payload_hash(payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
+    """SHA-256 over contracts.audit's canonical RunEvent JSON.
+
+    ``contracts.audit.recompute_payload_hash`` uses Pydantic
+    ``model_dump(mode="json")`` plus ``json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True,
+    separators=(",", ":"))``. UTC datetimes therefore render with a trailing
+    ``Z``. Keep this byte-compatible; otherwise an outbox event that is valid
+    for the risk gate is rejected by E's verify_payload/replay.
+    """
+    canonical = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
+    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

@@ -0,0 +1,275 @@
+"""Pack-level evidence assembly for FR-01 / INV-02 (module A).
+
+``build_pack`` turns raw provider items into an immutable :class:`EvidencePack`
+and its :class:`~egta.contracts.ExcludedItem` list; ``validate_claims`` fails
+closed on a claim that cites an evidence id the pack does not contain.
+
+# Implements: FR-01 (evidence pack), INV-02 (point-in-time admissibility)
+
+Design decisions frozen by the approved pack-level spec
+(``test/offline/evidence/test_pack.py``, PR #25) and its trace:
+
+* ``pack_hash`` is **computed here**, never supplied by a caller. It is the SHA-256
+  of the canonical ``evidence_fields(pack)`` and therefore equals
+  :func:`egta.contracts.canonical.recompute_evidence_hash`; the risk gate recomputes
+  and rejects any mismatch as ``INTEGRITY_VIOLATION`` (``test_pack_hash_matches_risk_gate_canonical``).
+* Claim citations use the **full** evidence id ``<run_id>-<case_local_id>``, matching
+  the risk gate's index (``risk_gate/rules.py`` ``_check_claims``).
+* A dangling citation raises :class:`InvalidCitation` carrying
+  ``ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION`` and naming the bad id.
+* ``source_type == "cache"`` is always stale (``STALE_DATA`` / ``stale``); there is
+  no age-based freshness threshold in this spec.
+* Classification order is integrity -> staleness -> time -> dedupe, so a tampered
+  cache item is ``INTEGRITY_VIOLATION`` and a future cache item is ``STALE_DATA``
+  (see ``_assemble`` and ``trace-FR-01-pack.md``).
+* ``pack.items`` preserves raw input order (admitted items only). A duplicate
+  (same ``source_uri`` + publication instant + ``content_hash``) is silently
+  collapsed, not listed as an exclusion.
+* A caller-supplied ``conflict_key`` groups *more than one* admitted item; a single
+  admitted item is never grouped.
+
+Pure time filtering (E-13..E-20, E-27, E-28, E-31) is owned by
+:func:`egta.evidence.time_policy.is_admissible`; this module only wires its verdicts
+into the pack.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
+from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
+from typing import Any
+
+from egta.contracts import Availability, EvidenceItem, EvidencePack, ExcludedItem, RunSpec
+from egta.contracts.canonical import recompute_evidence_hash
+from egta.contracts.events import ReasonCode
+from egta.evidence.time_policy import is_admissible
+
+_TIME_GRANULARITY_NONE = "none"
+_INTEGRITY_AVAILABILITY = Availability.UNAVAILABLE
+_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ID = "provider"
+_HASH_ZERO = "0" * 64
+
+
+class InvalidCitation(Exception):
+    """A claim cites an evidence id absent from the pack (``INVALID_CITATION``).
+
+    Carries the offending id so callers can report precisely which citation was
+    dangling without re-parsing the message.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, evidence_id: str) -> None:
+        self.evidence_id = evidence_id
+        self.reason_code = ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION
+        super().__init__(
+            f"{ReasonCode.INVALID_CITATION.value}: claim cites unknown evidence id "
+            f"{evidence_id!r}"
+        )
+
+
+def _sha256_hex(text: str) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _publication_instant(published_at: Any) -> Any:
+    """Normalize ``published_at`` for dedupe keys only (never mutates the item).
+
+    Date-only values collapse to their ``date``; aware datetimes to UTC; naive and
+    malformed values are kept verbatim so distinct bad values stay distinct.
+    """
+    if isinstance(published_at, datetime):
+        return published_at.astimezone(UTC) if published_at.tzinfo is not None else published_at
+    if isinstance(published_at, date):
+        return published_at
+    if isinstance(published_at, str):
+        try:
+            parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(published_at.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+        except ValueError:
+            return published_at
+        return parsed.astimezone(UTC) if parsed.tzinfo is not None else parsed
+    return published_at
+
+
+def _raw_get(raw: Mapping[str, Any], key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
+    return raw.get(key, default)
+
+
+def _is_cache(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    return _raw_get(raw, "source_type") == "cache"
+
+
+def _is_tampered(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    excerpt = _raw_get(raw, "excerpt")
+    content_hash = _raw_get(raw, "content_hash")
+    if not isinstance(excerpt, str) or not isinstance(content_hash, str):
+        return False
+    return _sha256_hex(excerpt) != content_hash
+
+
+def _dedupe_key(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Any, Any, Any]:
+    return (
+        _raw_get(raw, "source_uri"),
+        _publication_instant(_raw_get(raw, "published_at")),
+        _raw_get(raw, "content_hash"),
+    )
+
+
+def _excluded(case_local_id: str, reason: ReasonCode, availability: Availability) -> ExcludedItem:
+    return ExcludedItem(
+        case_local_id=case_local_id,
+        availability=availability,
+        reason_code=reason,
+    )
+
+
+def _to_evidence_item(
+    run_id: str,
+    raw: Mapping[str, Any],
+    *,
+    conflict_group: str | None,
+) -> EvidenceItem:
+    return EvidenceItem(
+        evidence_id=f"{run_id}-{raw['case_local_id']}",
+        source_uri=raw["source_uri"],
+        published_at=raw["published_at"],
+        fetched_at=raw["fetched_at"],
+        content_hash=raw["content_hash"],
+        excerpt=raw["excerpt"],
+        availability=Availability.AVAILABLE,
+        trust_label=raw["trust_label"],
+        reason_code=None,
+        conflict_group=conflict_group,
+    )
+
+
+def _time_verdict(raw: Mapping[str, Any], run_spec: RunSpec):
+    granularity = _raw_get(raw, "time_granularity", _TIME_GRANULARITY_NONE)
+    return is_admissible(
+        published_at=_raw_get(raw, "published_at"),
+        time_granularity=granularity if isinstance(granularity, str) else _TIME_GRANULARITY_NONE,
+        as_of=run_spec.as_of,
+    )
+
+
+def _assemble(
+    run_spec: RunSpec,
+    raw_items: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    *,
+    provider_error: Any,
+    conflict_key: str | None,
+) -> tuple[list[EvidenceItem], list[ExcludedItem]]:
+    exclusions: list[ExcludedItem] = []
+
+    if provider_error is not None:
+        exclusions.append(
+            _excluded(_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ID, ReasonCode.VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE, Availability.UNREACHABLE)
+        )
+
+    admitted_raw: list[Mapping[str, Any]] = []
+    seen: set[tuple[Any, Any, Any]] = set()
+
+    # Precedence (frozen by trace-FR-01-pack.md "classification rule"):
+    #   1. integrity  — a hash/excerpt mismatch is INTEGRITY_VIOLATION regardless
+    #      of source_type, so a *tampered cache item* is reported as tampering, not
+    #      silently downgraded to STALE (audit correctness for FR-01/T04).
+    #   2. staleness  — a well-formed ``source_type == "cache"`` item is always
+    #      STALE_DATA/stale (frozen E-26 rule; no age threshold).
+    #   3. time       — INV-02 point-in-time admissibility via time_policy.
+    #   4. dedupe     — collapse identical (uri, publication instant, content_hash).
+    # A future-dated *cache* item therefore classifies as STALE at step 2 (cache is
+    # unverifiable off-line) rather than FUTURE_DATA at step 3; a future-dated
+    # *non-cache* item classifies as FUTURE_DATA at step 3.
+    for raw in raw_items:
+        local_id = _raw_get(raw, "case_local_id")
+        if _is_tampered(raw):
+            exclusions.append(
+                _excluded(local_id, ReasonCode.INTEGRITY_VIOLATION, _INTEGRITY_AVAILABILITY)
+            )
+            continue
+        if _is_cache(raw):
+            exclusions.append(_excluded(local_id, ReasonCode.STALE_DATA, Availability.STALE))
+            continue
+        verdict = _time_verdict(raw, run_spec)
+        if not verdict.admissible:
+            exclusions.append(
+                _excluded(local_id, ReasonCode(verdict.reason_code), Availability.UNAVAILABLE)
+            )
+            continue
+        key = _dedupe_key(raw)
+        if key in seen:
+            # Silent collapse: a duplicate is neither admitted nor an exclusion.
+            continue
+        seen.add(key)
+        admitted_raw.append(raw)
+
+    group = conflict_key if (conflict_key is not None and len(admitted_raw) > 1) else None
+    items = [
+        _to_evidence_item(run_spec.run_id, raw, conflict_group=group) for raw in admitted_raw
+    ]
+    return items, exclusions
+
+
+def _pack_with_hash(
+    run_spec: RunSpec,
+    items: list[EvidenceItem],
+    exclusions: list[ExcludedItem],
+) -> EvidencePack:
+    # Build with a placeholder, then bind pack_hash to the canonical recomputation
+    # over the pack's evidence_fields. recompute_evidence_hash ignores pack_hash, so
+    # the placeholder never affects the digest.
+    provisional = EvidencePack(
+        run_id=run_spec.run_id,
+        snapshot_id=run_spec.snapshot_id,
+        items=items,
+        excluded_items=exclusions,
+        cutoff=run_spec.as_of,
+        pack_hash=_HASH_ZERO,
+    )
+    pack_hash = recompute_evidence_hash(provisional)
+    return provisional.model_copy(update={"pack_hash": pack_hash})
+
+
+def build_pack(
+    run_spec: RunSpec,
+    raw_items: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    *,
+    provider_error: Any = None,
+    conflict_key: str | None = None,
+) -> EvidencePack:
+    """Assemble an :class:`EvidencePack` from raw provider items (FR-01 / INV-02).
+
+    ``provider_error`` (any non-``None`` value) records a single provider-level
+    exclusion (``VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE`` / ``unreachable``). ``conflict_key`` marks a
+    caller-known conflict group across all admitted items when more than one
+    remains after filtering/dedupe.
+    """
+    items, exclusions = _assemble(
+        run_spec,
+        raw_items,
+        provider_error=provider_error,
+        conflict_key=conflict_key,
+    )
+    return _pack_with_hash(run_spec, items, exclusions)
+
+
+def _claim_evidence_ids(claim: Any) -> Iterable[str]:
+    if isinstance(claim, Mapping):
+        return claim.get("evidence_ids", ()) or ()
+    return getattr(claim, "evidence_ids", ()) or ()
+
+
+def validate_claims(pack: EvidencePack, claims: Iterable[Any]) -> None:
+    """Fail closed if any claim cites an evidence id absent from ``pack``.
+
+    Raises :class:`InvalidCitation` naming the first dangling id. Accepts claim
+    mappings or objects exposing ``evidence_ids`` (full ``<run_id>-<case_local_id>``
+    ids, matching the risk gate's index).
+    """
+    known = {item.evidence_id for item in pack.items}
+    for claim in claims:
+        for evidence_id in _claim_evidence_ids(claim):
+            if evidence_id not in known:
+                raise InvalidCitation(str(evidence_id))
+
+
+__all__ = ["InvalidCitation", "build_pack", "validate_claims"]

 def connect(db_path: str | Path, busy_timeout_seconds: float) -> sqlite3.Connection:
     connection = sqlite3.connect(
         str(Path(db_path)),
         timeout=busy_timeout_seconds,
         isolation_level=None,
     )
     connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
     connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
     connection.execute(f"PRAGMA busy_timeout = {int(busy_timeout_seconds * 1000)}")
     return connection
 
 
 def initialize(db_path: str | Path, portfolio: Any) -> None:
     connection = connect(db_path, 5.0)
     try:
         connection.executescript(_SCHEMA)
         existing = connection.execute(
             "SELECT 1 FROM portfolios WHERE portfolio_id = ?",
             (portfolio.portfolio_id,),
         ).fetchone()
         if existing is None:
             connection.execute(
                 "INSERT INTO portfolios "
                 "(portfolio_id, version, base_currency, cash, as_of) "
                 "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                 (
                     portfolio.portfolio_id,
                     int(portfolio.version),
                     portfolio.base_currency,
                     str(portfolio.cash),
                     portfolio.as_of.isoformat(),
                 ),
             )
             for position in portfolio.positions:
                 connection.execute(
                     "INSERT INTO positions "
                     "(portfolio_id, symbol, quantity, mark_price) "
                     "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                     (
                         portfolio.portfolio_id,
                         position.symbol,
                         int(position.quantity),
                         str(position.mark_price),
                     ),
                 )
         connection.execute(
             "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO schema_meta (key, value) VALUES ('schema_version', '1')"
         )
         connection.commit()
     finally:

     connection: sqlite3.Connection,

     new_version: int,
     cash_after: Decimal,
     position_symbol: str,
     position_after: int,

 ) -> None:
